_description: English translation of the COSMOS installation and removal dialogue. The Russian file messages-ru.json is the source; every key here matches it exactly. %s in a string is a substitution — its order and count must not be changed.
ui.need_number: Please enter a number from 1 to %s (or just press Enter).
ui.no_input: nothing was entered — the default was used
ui.press_enter: Press Enter to close this window.
inst.title: COSMOS Installer
inst.decisions_done: decisions: %s | determined by the program: %s | asked: %s
inst.report_failed: the report could not be written (%s) — this does not affect the installation
inst.journal: installation log (needed in order to remove the program): %s
run.starting: Starting the program and waiting for it to respond…
run.started: The program is running. Opening it in your browser: %s
run.start_failed: The program did not respond within %s seconds. You can start it later with the file %s — the window that opens will show what happened.
run.start: To start it: double-click the file %s
run.address: The program will open in your browser at %s
run.address_lan: From other computers on this network: %s
run.password: Sign in with the password shown above.
run.stop: To stop it: close the window that opened when you started the program.
run.solver: Rostering (stage 2) needs a separate service of its own: %s
run.uninstall: To remove the program: double-click UNINSTALL-COSMOS.cmd, or run %s
q.target: Where should COSMOS be installed? (the folder will be created)
q.go: Install the program according to this plan?
q.linux_ack: This computer is not running Windows. The application has been checked with the full set of tests on Windows; on Linux the build is marked as optional and it has not been proven to work there. Continue?
q.contour: Allow artificial intelligence models in the cloud on this installation?
q.contour.internal: no — this is a site with a strict policy: every artificial intelligence suggestion is prepared by a local model only
q.contour.external: yes — for data sets marked as open data; customer data sets (marked "local only", which is the default setting) are never sent to the cloud
q.api_key: Key for the cloud model (press Enter to skip and enter it later in the Settings section)
q.ollama_url: The local artificial intelligence model (Ollama) is not answering at the usual address. It is needed for suggestions about customer data: such data sets are never sent to the cloud. If the server runs on another computer or on another port, enter its address, for example http://192.168.1.50:11434. If there is no such server, just press Enter.
q.ollama_model: Which local model should be used? The quality and the speed of the suggestions depend on this choice.
warn.ollama_silent: The local model server at %s did not answer.
warn.no_local_model: IMPORTANT: there is no local model. Artificial intelligence suggestions about customer data will not work — such data sets are marked "local only" and are not sent to the cloud. The program itself is fully usable: the pairing and rostering calculations do not depend on artificial intelligence models. You can install a local model later and enter it in the Settings section.
q.auth: How will people sign in to the program?
q.auth.token: with a password — the program creates it on first start and shows it to you; it works straight away and needs no outside services
q.auth.access: with a one-time code sent to a work email address — this needs a Cloudflare account (a free one is enough) with Zero Trust set up and the program published to the outside world through their tunnel; if you do not have that, choose the password option
q.net: Which computers should be able to open the program?
q.net.lan: every computer on this local network (it will not be reachable from the internet)
q.access_team: The name of your organisation in Cloudflare — the part of the address before .cloudflareaccess.com. If your sign-in page looks like mycompany.cloudflareaccess.com, enter: mycompany
q.access_aud: Application identifier (the AUD string). Where to find it: Cloudflare dashboard → Zero Trust → Access → Applications → your application → Overview tab → Application Audience (AUD) Tag field — copy the whole value
q.super_admin: Email address of the super administrator (several allowed, comma-separated; the first one is the super administrator)
q.install_toolchain: Not found: %s — without these, stage 2 (rostering) will not work. Download them from the official sources (Adoptium and Apache), check the checksum and unpack them INTO THE INSTALLATION FOLDER? Your system is not changed, administrator rights are not needed, and the download is about 200 MB.
q.autostart: Start the program automatically when the computer starts up (%s)?
step.rules: rules file created from the sample
res.manifest.failed: the inventory could not be written (%s) — the removal will be more cautious, but it will still work
verify.answer: response from the application (startup file, port %s)
verify.password_title: PASSWORD FOR SIGNING IN TO THE PROGRAM:  %s
verify.password_where: Write it down. It is also kept in the file
verify.password_reset: If you forget the password: delete the file
verify.password_reset2: and start the program again — it will create a new one.
key.no_access: This computer does not yet have access to the source code.
key.easy: This can be put right in a couple of minutes and needs nothing complicated.
key.failed: The key could not be created: %s
key.send: Send this whole line to the person who grants access (the owner of the repository). They will add it in the settings: Settings → Deploy keys → Add deploy key, without write permission.
key.wait: When the owner confirms that the key has been added, press Enter.
un.title: COSMOS Removal
un.journal_interrupted: the installation was INTERRUPTED — removing whatever had already been created
un.journal_missing: There is no installation log — what to remove is worked out from indirect signs (the marker in the startup file, a comparison of the folder tree, a rule for picking out processes). This way is less exact.
un.dry_notice: Nothing will be changed. To carry the removal out for real, add --apply.
un.manifest_found: the inventory of the installation was found: %s objects — there are no blind zones, every one of them is checked
un.manifest_missing: there is no inventory of the installation — parts of the folder tree are accepted without a file-by-file comparison
un.keep_ssh: NOT removed (may have been added to other repositories): key %s
un.nothing_to_remove: nothing to remove: %s is not there
un.would_remove: [trial run] this would have been removed: %s
un.empty_left: all the contents have been removed; the empty folder %s is still held by the system and will disappear once this removal program has finished
un.mentions: (left alone, it only mentions the path): PID %s
un.would_stop: [trial run] PID %s would have been stopped
un.unknown_port: the port is not known — this step was not carried out
un.dry_ok: trial run: all checks passed, nothing was changed
un.confirm: Remove COSMOS from this computer? This cannot be undone: the password for signing in and the program's log will be destroyed.
un.result.done: RESULT: the removal has been carried out
un.result.dry: RESULT: the checks passed, you can now run it with --apply
un.stop_tail: Nothing has been removed beyond what is printed above. The decision is up to the owner.
un.list.none: No installation logs were found in %s
un.task_no_name: scheduler task: the name is not known — this step was not carried out
un.rule_no_name: firewall rule: the name is not known — this step was not carried out
un.would_remove_task: [trial run] the scheduler task %s would have been removed
un.would_remove_rule: [trial run] the firewall rule "%s" would have been removed
un.rule_preexisting: the firewall rule "%s" existed BEFORE the installation — it is left alone
un.journal_kept: the installation log has been kept for the record: %s
un.left.processes: processes of the installation are still running: %s
gate.scope_journal: what to remove, from the log
gate.scope_signs: what to remove, from indirect signs
gate.foreign_content: items that do not belong, by content
gate.foreign_time: items that do not belong, by date
cnt.name: name
stop.foreign: items that do not belong to the installation were found in its folder (%s of them): the owner may have MOVED a file of their own here
stop.older: the folder contains objects older than the installation itself — they may have been moved here, and removing them would destroy the original
stop.links: links were found (%s of them): a person created them, and only that person has the right to decide what they are for
stop.hardlinks: read-only files that have more than one name (%s of them): removing them would ruin someone else's original file
stop.data_not_empty: the data folder is not empty — this is the owner's data
stop.catalog_queues: please move the template catalog request queues elsewhere: %s — they are created by the programs at work, not by the installation, and they must not be removed blind
stop.no_marker: %s holds no installer marker and there is no installation log either — it has not been proven where this folder came from
stop.incomplete: the removal is not complete: %s still exists (objects: %s)
stop.own_console: the removal was started from the very console that runs the installation (PID %s): stopping it would mean killing itself. Please start it from a separate window.
stop.enum_error: error while listing the folder tree (%s items)
stop.pid_reused: PID %s now belongs to a different process
stop.postcheck: the check after removal found differences
stop.read_dir_failed: the folder %s could not be read: %s
stop.read_attrs_failed: the properties of %s could not be read: %s
stop.ps_failed: the list of processes could not be obtained: %s
stop.fw_state_unknown: it could not be established whether the firewall rule "%s" exists: %s
stop.task_state_unknown: it could not be established whether the scheduler task "%s" exists: %s
stop.no_evidence: for %s neither a comparison against the version control system nor a comparison by date is possible — removing it blind is not allowed
stop.task_elsewhere: the scheduler task %s does not lead to %s: %s
probe.os.unproven: %s  — this platform has been tested less
probe.admin.no: no — automatic start will need them
probe.venv.absent: not there — the environment cannot be created
probe.pypi.fail: not reachable — the dependencies cannot be installed (%s)
probe.git.absent: not found — the source code will have to be brought over by hand
probe.repo.no_git: git was not found — there is nothing to check the access with
probe.repo.ok: the repository can be read — cloning will work
probe.repo.need_key: this computer needs access to the private repository: add its public SSH key as a deploy key (Settings → Deploy keys) and give an address of the form git@github.com:<owner>/<repository>.git
probe.repo.no_helper: the credential helper is not available in this session (there is no interactive sign-in) — signing in through a browser will not work here, an SSH key is needed
probe.repo.not_found: no repository was found at this address
probe.jdk.absent: not found — stage 2 (rostering) will not work
probe.jdk.old: version %s — version %s or newer is needed
probe.maven.absent: not found — the solver will have to be built separately
probe.ollama.silent: no answer at %s — artificial intelligence suggestions will be switched off
probe.ollama.no_models: the server is there, but it has no models
probe.cloudflared.ok: present — signing in through Cloudflare Access is possible
probe.cloudflared.absent: not found — signing in will be local
probe.ports_free.none: there are no free ports in the range %s-%s
probe.target.busy: %s — the folder IS NOT EMPTY (this will be an update, not a fresh installation)
probe.target.readonly: %s — there is no permission to write there
probe.disk.low: %s GB — at least %s GB is needed
why.site.proven: a platform that has been tested
why.site.unproven_ok: a platform that has not been tested: continuing was confirmed
why.site.unproven_no: a platform that has not been tested: continuing was NOT confirmed
why.port.flag: the port was given when the installer was started
why.port.taken: port %s is taken, the nearest free one was used instead
why.data_scope: the program cannot work out the policy of this site by itself; the protection of customer data holds in both cases — the mark is set on every data set
why.model.single: the server has only one model
why.model.choice: the choice of model affects the quality and the speed of the suggestions
why.model.none: there is no server of local models
why.ollama_url: a server of local models answers at this address
why.model_default: worked out from the data policy and from whether a local server is present
why.api_key.external: an external installation may use a cloud model
why.api_key.internal: an internal installation: a cloud model is not allowed, so no key is needed
why.auth.token: the program creates the password on first start
why.auth.access: signing in with a code sent to an email address was chosen
why.net: the program cannot work out by itself which computers should see it — this is the owner's decision
why.access: the sign-in pass is checked against it
why.super_admin: the first address can open the Settings section; every listed address becomes an administrator on first start
why.toolchain.present: already on this computer — there is nothing to install
why.toolchain.allowed: downloading from the network needs permission
why.toolchain.denied: not allowed: stage 1 (pairing) works, stage 2 (rostering) will stay unavailable
why.solver.ready: JDK %s and Maven were found — stage 2 will be built
why.solver.will_build: the solver will be built with the set of tools that was downloaded
why.autostart.allowed: a change to the system needs permission
why.autostart.no_admin: there are no administrator rights, so it cannot be registered
why.workers: from the number of cores, two are left to the system
why.lang: the first question of the installation; it becomes the language of the program
res.deps.ok: the dependencies were installed from pyproject.toml
res.rules.created: created from the sample — CHECK the values against the customer's own: %s
res.toolchain.maven_nosha: Maven %s (no sha256 checksum has been published)
res.solver.skipped: skipped: JDK 21 or Maven is missing (stage 2 will not be available)
res.solver.built_local_jdk: the solver has been built (with the JDK from the installation folder)
res.firewall.skipped: skipped: access from this computer only
res.firewall.linux: on Linux, add the firewall rule with the tools of your distribution (for example ufw allow from <subnet> to any port %s)
res.firewall.created: rule "%s": incoming connections from the local subnet are allowed
res.solver_launcher.skipped: skipped: the solver has not been built
verify.note.venv: the interpreter of the environment was not found: %s
verify.note.answer: the application did not answer on port %s; the end of the log: %s
verify.note.no_password: the password for signing in was not found in the log — if signing in does not work, delete webapp/config/auth.json and start the program again
rep.title: Report on the COSMOS installation
rep.secrets: Secrets are not written into the report — only the mark "set".
rep.envvars.body: CREW_TASK_PACKAGE — path to the task package (manifest with the VMP readiness matrix; without it the main screen honestly shows "package not connected"). CREW_VMP_REGISTRY — path to the VMP executor registry (without it runs on a task package are stopped by the conformance gate). CREW_DATA_DIR — relocates the data directory (default is the sibling "<target>-data"). CREW_CPLEX_EXE — path to the external CPLEX solver (optional: the cplex selection engine refuses honestly without it).
run.cdpm: The CDPM formalization module runs as its own service: %s
res.cdpm_launcher.skipped: skipped: the data module is not in the installation folder
res.catalog_launcher.skipped: skipped: the catalog service is not in the installation folder
run.catalog: The template catalog opens as its own service (view only): %s, address %s
verify.catalog.skipped: the catalog service is not part of the kit - skipped
verify.catalog.answer: response of the catalog service (startup file, port %s)
verify.note.catalog: the catalog service did not answer on port %s; log tail: %s
verify.note.catalog_check: the template catalog was not checked: %s
verify.catalog.bridge_skipped: the CDPM bridge is not part of the kit - skipped
verify.note.catalog_bridge: the CDPM bridge did not read the template catalog: %s
step.layout: role model layout created from the sample
res.layout.created: created from the sample — CHECK the role models against the customer's needs (without a layout the cloud stages of the data processing module do not start): %s
probe.cplex.found: found: %s — the cplex engine is available; by default the calculation runs on CP-SAT
probe.cplex.absent: not found — the calculation runs on CP-SAT (the default engine); the installer does not install CPLEX
probe.venv.no_ensurepip: the venv module is present but without ensurepip — the environment cannot be created; install the python3-venv package (for example: sudo apt install python3-venv)
verify.note.catalog_port: the catalog service startup file names no port (--port): %s - the response was not checked
verify.note.catalog_port_mismatch: catalog service port mismatch: the check was told %s, the startup file starts the service on %s - the response was not checked
why.catalog_port.default: the default catalog service port (%s); another one — with --catalog-port
